subject: Ternus' First Test As Apple CEO

 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 Trade war: The U.S. targets Canadian alcohol, dairy and motorcycles in latest retaliatory tariffs.

 'Troubling picture': Ford's ( F ) ties with Chinese firms CATL and Geely face U.S. scrutiny .

 Safety fears:  Anthropic ( ANTHRO ) staff warn of self-improving AI that could spiral out of control.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 New era 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
Tech enthusiasts and Wall Street are tuning in ahead of Apple's ( AAPL ) big product event today, which will be the first device lineup showcased since John Ternus took the helm. The stakes are high, with the design veteran expected to herald a new era of innovation at Apple.

 What to expect:  "Apple's 'Surprise and Shine' product launch event should follow a similar format to past years — a 90-minute presentation of Apple's newest device introductions, namely the Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4, AirPods 5, iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max, and, most importantly, its first foldable iPhone," Morgan Stanley noted. Perhaps the most consequential part of the event will be  Ternus' keynote speech , which Forrester analyst Dipanjan Chatterjee  said will set the tone for the CEO's vision of Apple's future. "Ternus inherits perhaps the most successful consumer technology juggernaut in modern times," Chatterjee said. "Tim Cook's perfected execution, scale, and monetization set a high bar, and Ternus must extend that run. But he must sustain that momentum while positioning Apple to disrupt itself in the near future." One product that signals the new era is the foldable iPhone, one of the most significant design changes for the smartphone. 

 Dig deeper:  Apple's core technology development teams have been exploring foldable phones for almost a decade, Bloomberg News reported, citing sources. Former CEO Tim Cook pushed for the foldable iPhone in 2020 after a trip to Asia, where people were using folding devices from Samsung ( SSNLF ) and other companies. To note, Samsung launched its first Galaxy Fold in 2019. Now Apple's first foldable device — called iPhone Duo — will reportedly be priced starting at $2,000 . That's more expensive than other foldable phones in the market, but it may not deter buyers. "Even with a $2,500 price tag, the Apple foldable is ​going to fly off the shelves, especially because Apple is excellent at creating an aura of exclusivity, luxury, and scarcity," Nabila Popal, senior research director ​at IDC, told Reuters .  Apple's next chapter: Measuring its stock gains since 1980 

 Bigger picture:  "We currently forecast ~6.5M foldable iPhone shipments in the December quarter, translating to ~$14B of revenue , or 16% of total December quarter iPhone revenue," Morgan Stanley estimated. "It will be worth watching how Apple leverages the larger form factor and whether it delivers use cases that are better on a foldable vs. simply a larger screen — and most importantly, how the device really feels in hand. If consumer reception is strong, we believe the category could ultimately become larger than current supply chain forecasts imply." SA analyst Tangerine Tan Capital thinks the foldable iPhone could be a sales success. "I like big screens for working on my iPhone, but they are sometimes too big for my pocket. So, a foldable iPhone sounds like a good idea to me," they said, but warned that the price tag could be too high for many .
